QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_42

answer.text: Making misleading or false statements, hiding material facts or key risk factors, misrepresentation/exaggeration, assuring returns, commission-driven mis-selling, and unsuitable recommendations

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM XIX-A (pp. 273-278), distributors are prohibited from making misleading statements, concealing or omitting material facts, hiding key risk factors, misrepresentation or exaggeration, omission or obfuscation by misleading investors, assuring returns, commission-driven mis-selling, and engaging in fraudulent or unfair trade practices. The Trap: Suitability assessment, transparent disclosure, and suitability-based recommendation are required good practices — not prohibited ones. Note: Even a well-intentioned recommendation becomes a violation if it suppresses risk or is driven primarily by commission rather than investor fit.
